intended_object: The canonical isomorphism, in the arrow category of schemes, between a morphism f : X → Y of affine schemes and the morphism Spec Γ(Y) → Spec Γ(X) induced by the ring map f^♯ : Γ(Y, O_Y) → Γ(X, O_X) on global sections. This comes from the docstring.
explanation: The body builds the arrow isomorphism with `Arrow.isoMk`. Its two components are the canonical isomorphisms `X.isoSpec : X ≅ Spec Γ(X)` and `Y.isoSpec : Y ≅ Spec Γ(Y)`. The required commuting square is naturality of the unit of the Γ–Spec adjunction. This is the standard fact that, for affine schemes, the morphism f is identified with Spec of its map on global sections, i.e. Spec is an anti-equivalence between affine schemes and rings. The construction needs X and Y to be affine, since otherwise `isoSpec` is not an isomorphism, so the generality is the natural one. It is a canonical isomorphism (data) that matches its docstring.
